data.title: Database Accessible Without Authentication
data.summary: Database and cache services were reachable over the network without authentication, or with default credentials, exposing their full contents to anyone able to connect.
data.description:
Several widely used data stores historically shipped listening on all interfaces with no authentication, on the assumption of a trusted network. That assumption fails in cloud deployments, in flat internal networks, and wherever a security group is opened for troubleshooting.

Exposure of this kind is total rather than partial: the attacker is not exploiting a flaw but using the product as designed, reading and writing every record. Caches and message queues are equally significant, since they hold session tokens and in-flight data.

These instances are found by internet-wide scanning within hours of exposure, and the data is routinely copied and ransomed.
data.recommendation:
* Bind data stores to internal interfaces only, and require authentication even there.
* Enforce network restrictions at the firewall or security group, scoped to the application tier.
* Use distinct accounts per application with least privilege, and rotate credentials.
* Enable encryption in transit and at rest.
* Alert on connections from unexpected sources.
data.short_recommendation: Bind databases to internal interfaces and require authentication.
